newsitem.title: ITALY: WFP halts most food aid in western Liberia.
newsitem.headline: WFP halts most food aid in western Liberia.

text.p: The World Food Programme said on Thursday that it had stopped distributing uncooked rations to tens of thousands of people in western Liberia because of the risk of attacks on civilians by faction fighters.

A statement by the WFP, the world's largest food aid agency, said only cooked food which could be eaten on the spot was now being handed out in Cape Mount County and the town of Tubmanburg, cutting the number of recipients to only about 2,500 people.
Distribution of uncooked food, so-called "dry food rations", would resume when security improved and recipients could carry rations away without being robbed, it said.
"The fighters harass the civilians, stealing food and any other commodities they have," the Rome-based agency's director in Liberia, Arnt Breivik, was quoted as saying.

"Although we are very concerned about the malnutrition levels in these parts of Liberia, we cannot put these people at risk," Breivik said. "Even the people themselves have asked us to stop giving them food because they are afraid."
The WFP and other relief agencies reached Cape Mount County and Tubmanburg in September after access had been cut off for months by fighting.
The statement said the agencies had distributed two-week rations to almost 40,000 hungry people in the areas last month.
Tubmanburg, a stronghold of warlord General Roosevelt Johnson's Krahn tribe, is at the heart of the most volatile region in Liberia, which has been devastated by civil war since December 1989.
More than 150,000 people have died in the conflict.
